intro.title: Buffer & encoding
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple program that creates and manipulates binary data using Node.js Buffers. You'll learn the core concept of encoding, which is how text is converted to and from binary data for storage or transmission. The main technologies involved are the Node.js Buffer class and common character encodings like UTF-8. By the end, you'll understand how to create buffers from strings, read their contents, and handle different encoding formats in your applications.
intro.usecase: Buffers and encoding are fundamental when handling binary data in Node.js applications, such as processing file uploads in web forms or APIs. For example, when users upload images or documents through a dashboard interface, Node.js uses buffers to temporarily store this binary data before saving it to disk or processing it further. Developers also rely on encoding conversions when reading configuration files, parsing network protocols, or working with databases that store binary data. Understanding buffers is crucial for building efficient file processing systems, streaming services, or any application that deals with raw data beyond plain text.
